exposure: health worker imposition of marital status access barriers
health worker imposition of spousal consent access barriers
health worker willingness to provide methods
health worker imposition of age/parity restrictions
outcome: health facility readiness to deliver family planning services
availability of specific family planning methods (short-acting, long-acting reversible, permanent)
health worker knowledge regarding family planning methods
health worker confidence in providing methods
health worker willingness to provide methods
health worker imposition of service access restrictions based on age/parity/marital status/spousal consent
cohort: The study included 152 public, private-not-for-profit, and private-for-profit health facilities and 261 health workers in urban east-central Uganda.
finding: The study revealed sub-optimal health facility readiness for family planning services (average score 46.7%) in urban east-central Uganda, with low availability of long-acting methods, frequent stock-outs, and a high proportion of health workers imposing access restrictions.
